properties.project_name: P2 -- open-space strip between Mission Creek and Channel St
properties.digitized_from: Traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street centerlines and all neighbouring mapped shapes along the creek corridor between Mission Creek and Channel St, which left a set of separate scraps of unclaimed land. Pier & Point, comparing them against Esri satellite imagery, picked two by hand and specified how to combine them: the paved/planted strip along the creek's near bank, and a paved path further southeast, separated from the first by a landscaping/tree strip not captured as its own piece.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-20 via the numbered real-gap-fragment technique established for P8 (see that record): generated a map of every disconnected real (street-buffer- and already-tracked-polygon-excluded) scrap of land in the creek/Channel St corridor between about where P8 hands off (near the roundabout) and the creek bend northeast of it. Two rounds of owner review (first pass, then a request to extend the view further northeast) converged on: fragment 7, truncated at its north edge along the same real line P8's fragment 4 was cut on (a line fit through the north corners of P8's fragments 34/41/17, confirmed colinear to ~5e-8 deg) -- at fragment 7's own longitude range this line lands almost exactly on its existing north boundary (matching to within ~0.00015 deg at the fragment's far corner), separating the real open water of Mission Creek (the ~9,854 sqm piece north of the line, discarded) from the real paved/planted strip along the near bank (~4,855 sqm, kept). The owner then specified translating fragment 9 (a separate paved path, ~7,932 sqm) north to merge with the truncated fragment 7, closing a real but narrow (~17-22m) planting-strip gap between the two rather than tracing that gap directly -- picked a 0.0002 deg (~22m) north shift, comfortably past the ~0.000156 deg (~17.3m) minimum needed for the two shapes to touch, for a clean overlapping seam rather than a knife-edge join. Final shape is the union of truncated-7 and shifted-9 (~12,224 sqm). PRE-CLIPPED 2026-09-20 against the real street buffer (src/street_geometry.py) before committing: the union (fragment 7 truncated + fragment 9 translated north) reached into a real paved area near the boat-dock access road at its northeast end -- join_approximate.py --strict flagged this as a 25% MAJOR CLIP, at the threshold where the checker asks for a direct look rather than trusting the auto-clip. Inspected directly against Esri satellite imagery: the removed area is a real paved road/driveway crossing plus the road-side verge, not a mispositioned trace, so committed the pre-clipped result (12,224 sqm -> 9,128 sqm) directly rather than relying on the pipeline's silent auto-clip every run. Splits into three pieces: the near-bank strip (4,977 sqm), the road-side strip that was fragment 9 (3,896 sqm), and a small separate grassy patch near the boat dock (255 sqm) that the clip revealed as disconnected from the other two. TRIMMED 2026-09-20: dropped the small (~255 sqm) disconnected triangle near the boat dock at P2's northeast end per the owner's review -- an artifact of the street clip, not real intended P2 open space. Final: 2 pieces, ~8,873 sqm. TRIMMED AGAIN 2026-09-20: the kept near-bank strip still had a thin (1-9m wide) spike continuing northeast past a natural waist (width narrows to ~1.1m at lat 37.7728) up to the edge of the analysis bbox -- the same 'weird thin edge' pattern flagged and removed elsewhere in this session (P8's fragment-4 spike, fragment 18's ribbon). Cut at that waist and dropped the spike (~619 sqm) per the owner's review. Final: 2 pieces, ~8,254 sqm. REVERTED THE STREET-CLIP 2026-09-20: the owner reviewed the clipped 2-piece result and pointed out it broke the continuity the fragment-9 translation was specifically meant to achieve -- the clip was correctly removing a real paved road, but that road runs almost the full length between the near-bank strip and the road-side strip, so clipping split one corridor into two disconnected pieces. Chosen fix (owner's pick among 3 options offered): set street_clip_exempt=true, the same opt-out already used for Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza -- this record represents the park-corridor CONCEPT, which crosses the road at grade, not today's paved-road extent. Reverted to the pre-clip, spike-trimmed continuous shape (single Polygon, ~11,652 sqm; the same waist-cut technique removed the same northeast spike directly from this unclipped version, at a very similar cut latitude -- 37.7730 instead of 37.7728). STATUS UPDATED 2026-09-20: owner confirmed P2 is under construction (planned -> under_construction), while P7/P9 remain planned and P10 remains complete. STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-30: under_construction -> existing, per the owner. Construction has not started: SF Recreation and Park's project page (checked 2026-09-30) gives 'Construction begins: Late 2026 / Early 2027' and 'Open to the Public: TBD'. The walkable part of P2 today is the existing Huffaker Park path and community garden, which the Mission Creek Park South Extension schematic design says will be preserved and incorporated ('the existing Huffaker Park path will remain in the same location and width while the paving material will be required to be improved to city standards'). So P2 is standing, not-yet-redeveloped open space, the site's 'existing' status; the expected construction start stays on the timeline as a future milestone. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, digitized_from reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE, AND KNOWINGLY DISPLACED -- fragment 9's real digitized position is ~17-22m south of where it's drawn here; the owner directed this shift to close a real gap (a planting/tree strip between two paved features) with a single deliberate translation rather than tracing that gap's own real edges. Fragment 7's kept portion is a real computed shape (street/creek/already-tracked-polygon-bounded), not hand-traced. Overlaps the already-tracked real 'Mission Creek Park' polygon (which the owner has directed be unioned to include this record and P8, per their own framing that Mission Creek Park will evolve to encompass P1+P2+P8) and may overlap the real Mission Creek Park -- east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge) record (P1) at its northeast end, near the edge of the analysis window used to generate the candidate fragments -- not reconciled with either. STREET-CLIP EXEMPT: this record deliberately claims area that includes today's real paved road crossing the corridor (a park-corridor concept, not today's satellite extent) -- same class of exception as Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza. Do not treat this as a mispositioned trace; it's an intentional choice to keep the corridor continuous rather than split by a road the park is meant to cross at grade.'; digitized_from: 'Real-gap-fragment technique: bbox.difference(street buffer, src/street_geometry.py)..difference(all already-tracked parcels/approx polygons) over the creek corridor between Mission Creek and Channel St yielded a numbered set of disconnected real scraps of unclaimed land; the owner, viewing the numbered map against Esri satellite imagery, picked fragment 7 (the paved/planted strip along the creek's near bank) and fragment 9 (a paved path further southeast, separated from 7 by a landscaping/tree strip not itself captured as its own fragment) and specified how to combine them.'. CORRECTED 2026-10-10 (boundary with the east reach, P1): the owner chose the striped crosswalk beside the Mission Creek Park Pavilion as the hand-off between P2 and Mission Creek Park -- east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge), with the crosswalk belonging to the east reach. P2 now ends at a straight line across the park, perpendicular to the creek's long axis, through the south-west end of the crosswalk's stripes in Esri World Imagery (viewed 2026-10-10). The ~220 m2 that overlapped the east reach was removed, and the strip of the east reach lying south-west of that line (~3,800 m2, hand-traced from imagery) was added to P2, so the two shapes now meet exactly along the line with no overlap or gap. The earlier shape is otherwise unchanged, including the deliberately displaced piece described in the caveat. CORRECTED 2026-10-11 (figures only; no change to the shape): the 2026-10-10 entry above gives the overlap with the east reach as '~220 m2' and the strip moved as 'about 3,800 m2'. Recomputed from the committed shapes (the files at the commit before b422c6f7 against the files after it; both outlines projected to UTM zone 10N, EPSG:32610, areas by shapely): the old east reach (14,296 m2) and the old P2 (11,630 m2) overlapped by 1,222 m2, not ~220 m2. The east reach lost 3,739 m2 (to 10,556 m2) and gained nothing; P2 lost nothing (under 0.01 m2) and gained 2,517 m2 (to 14,147 m2), which is the 3,739 m2 moved less the 1,222 m2 P2 already covered. The two new shapes share no area. So the sentence above that P2 'loses the ~220 m2 that overlapped it' was wrong: P2 lost no area, and the overlap sits inside the part it gained and kept. The same recomputation finds the whole of this shape (14,147 m2) inside the 'Mission Creek Park' shape, the overlap the caveat already says is not reconciled. Earlier entries above are unedited. CHECKED 2026-10-11: the owner chose to keep this drawing and cite the Assessor lots under it. The owner reads lot 3810006 (16,093 m2, active, Channel St 202) as covering both P1 and the already built Huffaker Park part of P2, and lot 8710002 (16,398 m2, active, recorded 1999-09-21) as covering the part of P2 not yet constructed and P5 (which has no shape of its own on this map). Against this drawing, lot 3810006 overlaps it by 7,982 m2 and lot 8710002 by 6,164 m2; the two lots together are about 32,500 m2 and run out over the creek and up the strip into P1, so neither is P2's own lot. Both lots also lie under the tracked Mission Creek Park, which already unions P1, P2 and P8. No change to the shape. 2026-10-11: text only. accuracy_caveat described an intention to merge this shape with Mission Creek Park and P8, which read as an internal note; it now says only that the overlap with the existing 'Mission Creek Park' shape is not reconciled. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type. 2026-10-11: text only. Public text that said 'the owner' (lots assigned, chosen, kept or read by the owner) now says Pier & Point, because readers would take 'owner' to mean the landowner. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type. 2026-10-12 accuracy audit follow-up (text only; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type): the audit asked whether 'existing' overstates P2 while its neighbour P8, covered by the same project, is planned. Re-read: Rec and Park's project page (sfrecpark.org/1833, undated) gives 'Construction begins, Late 2026 / Early 2027' and 'Open to the Public, TBD' (both expected dates) and says 'This final segment of Mission Creek Park will provide 5.7 additional acres of new open space west of the Mission Creek Park Pavilion'; OCII's Nov 14, 2024 CAC update (p.2 map) labels 'MISSION CREEK PARK P2 & P8 coming soon' in the planned-park colour. No source read says construction has started as of 2026-10-12. The 2026-09-30 entry above bases 'existing' on the Huffaker Park path and garden that stand on P2 today and will be preserved; the status describes that existing open space, not the planned park, and the notes now say so. Status is left as set on 2026-09-30.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE, AND KNOWINGLY DISPLACED -- one of the two pieces making up this shape (the paved path further southeast) really lies about 17-22 m south of where it is drawn here; Pier & Point shifted it on purpose to close a real gap (a planting/tree strip between two paved features) with a single deliberate move rather than tracing that gap's own edges. The other piece (the strip along the creek's near bank) is a computed shape bounded by streets, the creek and neighbouring mapped shapes, not hand-traced. Overlaps the existing 'Mission Creek Park' shape; the map does not yet reconcile that overlap with this record or with P8. Meets the Mission Creek Park -- east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge) record (P1) exactly along a line through the south-west end of the striped crosswalk beside the Pavilion (the crosswalk belongs to the east reach). Deliberately not trimmed back from the street lines: this record includes area covering today's paved road across the corridor (a park-corridor concept, not today's satellite extent) -- the same kind of exception as Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza. This is not a mispositioned trace; it is an intentional choice to keep the corridor continuous rather than split by a road the park is meant to cross at grade. Pier & Point chose to keep this drawing and cite the Assessor lots under it. Pier & Point reads lot 3810006 (16,093 m2, active, Channel St 202) as covering both P1 and the already built Huffaker Park part of P2, and lot 8710002 (16,398 m2, active, recorded 1999-09-21) as covering the part of P2 not yet constructed and P5 (which has no shape of its own on this map). Against this drawing, lot 3810006 overlaps it by 7,982 m2 and lot 8710002 by 6,164 m2; the two lots together are about 32,500 m2 and run out over the creek and up the strip into P1, so neither is P2's own lot. Both lots also lie under the tracked Mission Creek Park, which already unions P1, P2 and P8.
properties.notes: OCII plan parcel P2. Runs along the near (south/west) bank of Mission Creek between the creek and Channel St, from about where P8 hands off near the Mission Bay Circle roundabout, northeast toward the creek bend. Sources: OCII's Dec 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map, which labels P2 on the south bank of Mission Creek (the label is in its text layer; colour and exact position were not re-checked), and SF Recreation and Park's Mission Creek Park South Extension project page, which says Parcels 2 and 8 will be a park along Mission Bay Drive and Channel Street that Rec and Park will own and operate. Today it holds the existing Huffaker Park path and a community garden, which Rec and Park's schematic design for the project says will be preserved and incorporated, with the path's paving brought up to city standards. Construction is expected to begin 'Late 2026 / Early 2027' per Rec and Park's project page (an expected date; the same page gives the opening as 'TBD', and no source read says construction has started). The 'existing' status describes only what stands there today, the Huffaker Park path and garden: the planned park on P2 and P8 is not built, OCII's Nov 14, 2024 CAC update map labels 'Mission Creek Park P2 & P8 coming soon' and shades it as planned park, and whether the whole parcel counts as an existing park is not clear from the sources read.
